2. Simulation configuration

Physics listFTFP_BERT_EMZ
Production cut0.01 mm
Crystalbox 10 × 10 × 10 mm
Surrounding mediumG4_AIR
Wrapper / finishdiffuse / polished
Sourcegamma pencil_beam, 662 keV, position [0, 0, -30] mm, direction [0, 0, 1]
Wall time524.0 s (single thread)
SensorSiPM on face +z, 6 × 6 mm², coupling layer

Physics implemented:

  • Gamma EM interactions via Geant4 reference physics list FTFP_BERT_EMZ (photoelectric, Compton, Rayleigh, pair production where kinematically allowed)
  • Secondary e-/e+/gamma transport with production cut 0.010000 mm
  • Scintillation: Geant4 G4Scintillation, yield linear in energy deposit; photon number Poisson (mean<=10) or Gaussian with sigma = resolution_scale*sqrt(mean) (mean>10)
  • Emission time: finite rise time and 1 exponential decay component(s)
  • Optical transport: bulk absorption, boundary process (Fresnel refraction/reflection, surface model unified)
  • Photodetection: wavelength-dependent PDE applied to each photon entering the sensor window (binomial photon counting)
  • Sensor timing: constant transit-time offset and Gaussian jitter per detected photon; Gaussian charge noise per event
  • SiPM microcell saturation (random cell per detected photon) with full dead-time recovery model

The complete configuration (including the original config.yaml text) is stored in summary.json, so the run is reproducible with the same seed.

7. Detector response

The energy resolution is dominated by position-dependent optical collection (spread 11.5%), not by photoelectron counting (≈2.2%). Changing reflector, surface finish, sensor size/position or absorption length will change it strongly.
Photopeak efficiency uses the window μ ± FWHM minus a fitted linear background; the truth full-energy fraction in Section 3 is an upper bound. They differ when the peak is broad or non-Gaussian (depth-dependent light collection produces a low-side tail).
Signal linearity: NOT evaluated — it needs simulations at several gamma energies (run ./run_all.sh --archive <tag> for each energy).

Reconstructed energy spectrum
Signal = fired microcells, scaled so the fitted photopeak sits at E_γ. Includes: yield statistics, optical collection variation, PDE statistics, SiPM saturation. Excludes electronics noise, nonproportionality, crosstalk/afterpulsing.

Effects included in the energy-resolution estimate: Scintillation yield statistics (Poisson); Optical collection variation (full Monte Carlo transport); Photodetection statistics (binomial PDE); SiPM microcell saturation with dead-time recovery.

Effects omitted (the simulated resolution is therefore optimistic): Scintillator nonproportionality / Birks quenching; Electronics noise, baseline, shaping; SiPM crosstalk, afterpulsing, dark counts; single-photon time jitter; Light-yield dependence on temperature.

Energy resolution (%) = (gamma photopeak FWHM [keV] / photopeak energy [keV]) × 100. This is unrelated to the emission-spectrum FWHM in nm.

8. Scientific limitations

  • Geant4 does not predict light yield, emission spectrum, decay times, absorption length or refractive index from composition. These are inputs.
  • Not modelled in this run:
    • Birks quenching and scintillation nonproportionality (yield is linear in deposited energy)
    • Cerenkov light
    • Temperature dependence of any property
    • Atomic fluorescence beyond what the production cut and physics list produce
    • Electronics baseline, shaping, digitisation (only Gaussian charge noise is applied)
    • SiPM optical crosstalk, afterpulsing, dark counts, PMT transit-time spread and gain fluctuations
    • Photons transmitted into the surrounding medium are discarded (counted as escaped); re-entry into the crystal is not modelled
    • Absorption in the optical coupling layer and sensor window (treated as transparent)
    • Wavelength-dependent reflectivity of the wrapper (constant or tabulated value used as given)
    • Self-absorption/re-emission (reabsorption without re-emission is represented by the absorption length only)
  • The crystal is a single idealised box; defects, inhomogeneity, surface damage and non-ideal wrapping are represented only through the supplied scalar/tabulated parameters.
  • Statistical uncertainties shown are Monte Carlo only; they do not include uncertainty in the inputs.

10. Final material evaluation

This is a factual summary of what was simulated. No overall good/bad score is assigned.

Material: CsPbBr3 (Cs1, Pb1, Br3), ρ = 4.86 g/cm³, T = 7 K.

Gamma interaction (662 keV): interaction fraction 0.3416 ± 0.0047, full-energy deposition fraction 0.1425 ± 0.0035 per emitted gamma; attenuation length 23.83 mm (calculated). These depend only on composition, density, geometry and source — they are the most trustworthy part of this report when those inputs are measured.

Scintillation: configured 50,000 photons/MeV (INPUT (literature)); the simulation generated 5.393e+04 photons per MeV deposited.

Optical transport: collection efficiency 0.146 ± 4.1e-05 (fraction of generated photons entering the sensor).

Photodetection: 2080 ± 6.4 photoelectrons for full-energy events.

Detector response: simulated energy resolution 21.00 ± 0.99 % at 662 keV (Gaussian fit; 1425 full-energy events). Because nonproportionality, electronics noise and other effects are omitted, this is a lower bound for what the same inputs would give in a real detector, not a prediction.
